Coding with agents is expensive. At Pedal, we use Claude for almost everything, and managing cost without interrupting my work has been a constant challenge. I hit session token limits and weekly and monthly spend caps, and I switch models, accounts and credit cards to avoid running out during important work.

This week, I analyzed my usage and found that much of my budget goes to work that is not client-facing and barely involves coding: cleanup, QA, reminders and documentation. Almost all of it is rote and repeated.

I designed a game for my agents to encourage them to use free, open source models instead of relying solely on paid Anthropic models.

Two chores moved from paid Claude calls to a free model running on my own machine (qwen3-coder:30b): sorting my inboxes and labeling GitHub issues. This page shows aggregates only: counts, dollars and milliseconds, never a message, sender or issue.
